A catered meal is defined as “a meal prepared in a commercial establishment for consumption there or delivered to a specific location or prepared at the consumption site using the caterer’s portable equipment and subsistence supplies.” There is no authority for a caterer to use Government-furnished equipment or Government-furnished facilities to prepare the meals. Caterers may locate a self-sustaining kitchen trailer or food truck at the requested location. Cooking tents and open/outdoor cooking are not authorized on location. Caterers preparing meals off site must ensure food safety precautions are adhered to at all times. Catered meals are authorized for the National Guard and Reserve Components in accordance with AR 30-22, Operating Procedures for the Army Food Program, Para 3-42. The caterer must provide personnel, supervision, and any items and services necessary to perform full catering services and in accordance with State and Local sanitation law requirements. All setup, serving, breakdown and cleanup will be the responsibility of the contractor. Contractor is not responsible for cleaning dining areas and kitchen areas. Contractor is responsible for cleaning serving lines if utilized. 1.3 Period of Performance (PoP): The Period of Performance must be for a duration of twelv

The Offeror shall submit a price for all line items below. Failure to do so may render the quote non-responsive. The Government anticipates being able to evaluate solely based upon lump sum prices quoted for each line item. However, the Government reserves the right to request breakdowns of any quoted lump sum prices, such as mobilization in and out, materials, labor, overhead, or profit. On lump sum line items, provide total price only. If no line item exists for a portion of the work, include the cost in a relative line item. In case of error in summation, the total of the corrected line-item amount governs. Round totals and extended prices to the nearest whole dollar (no cents). Award will be made to one contractor in accordance with solicitation. In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) provision, 52.204-07, Quoters must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number and an active registration in the System for Award Management database (SAM.gov) at time of submitting quote. equirements: FAR 52.203-3, Gratuities (Apr 1984): Prohibits contractors from offering gratuities to government personnel. Important for maintaining ethical standards. FAR 52.203-5, Covenant Against Contingent Fees (May 2014): Ensures the contractor didn't use improper influence to win the contract. FAR 52.204-13, System for Award Management Maintenance (Oct 2018): Requires contractors to maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). This is essential for receiving payments. FAR 52.204-18, Commercial and Government Entity Code Maintenance (Jul 2016): Requires maintenance of a valid CAGE code. FAR 52.215-2, Audit and Records—Negotiation (Jun 2020): Grants the government access to the contractor's records for auditing purposes, particularly important for cost-reimbursement or complex contracts. FAR 52.217-2, Cancellation Under Multi-Year Contracts (Oct 1995): If this could become a multi-year contract, this protects the government's right to cancel future years. FAR 52.219-28, Post-Award Small Business Program Representation (Sep 2021): Allows the contractor to update its small business status after award. Labor & Safet

The classifications are listed in alphabetical order under rate identifiers indicating whether the particular rate is a union rate (current union negotiated rate), a survey rate, a weighted union average rate, a state adopted rate, or a supplemental classification rate. Union Rate Identifiers A four-letter identifier beginning with characters other than SU , UAVG , SA , or SC denotes that a union rate was prevailing for that classification in the survey. Example: PLUM0198-005 07/01/2024. PLUM is an identifier of the union whose collectively bargained rate prevailed in the survey for this classification, which in this example would be Plumbers. 0198 indicates the local union number or district council number where applicable, i.e., Plumbers Local 0198. The next number, 005 in the example, is an internal number used in processing the wage determination. The date, 07/01/2024 in the example, is the effective date of the most current negotiated rate. award_criteria.text: A Commercial Solutions Opening W912CH- 25-S-C001. The Center for Army Analysis (CAA) seeks proposals for an innovative Information Technology (IT) services solution to enhance agency-wide IT and desktop support across its internally managed classified Closed Restricted Network (CRN) and its externally managed classified and unclassified network environments. Offerors shall provide a detailed narrative demonstrating their organizational capacity and a proven record of delivering effective, efficient support services comparable in scope to this requirement. The narrative must include specific examples of service delivery models, internal quality control measures, and a summary of historical performance metrics achieved for clients of comparable size and complexity. This CSO AoI seeks to solicit innovative solutions that meet the objectives detailed in Sections 1.2 and 1.3. The term innovative is defined as any technology, process, or method, including research and development that is new as of the date of proposal submission, or any new application of an existing technology, process or method as of the proposal date. Offerors are encouraged to submit multiple options. ACC-DTA is not obligated to extend a request for proposal or make an award as a result of this CSO AoI; all awards are subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. This CSO AoI is not an authorization to begin performance, and in no way obligates the Government for any costs incurred by the Offeror associated with developing a Response. Prior to commencement of any activities associated with performance under this CSO AoI, the Government will issue a written directive or contractual document signed by the Contracting Officer with appropriate consideration established. Under this CSO, the DoD may seek solution briefs, presentations/pitches, and/or proposals from traditional and nontraditional business entities for innovative commercial products, technologies, and services, or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial products, technologies, and services to meet U.S. Army needs and improve readiness. These include, but are not limited to, IT modernization, enhanced cybersecurity, efficient artifact restoration and conservation, streamlined base operations, and improved facility support. This CSO may result in the award of various types of contracts, which may include, but are not limited to, commercially-available products, technologies, or services immediately available; commercially-available products, technologies, or services fueled by commercial or strategic investment; and concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial products, technologies, or services, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for broad defense applications. The G

ars have been reserved for awards under this CSO. The participating DoD agencies will provide no funding for direct reimbursement of white paper or proposal development costs. NOTE: During any step of the CSO, the Government may send written questions or comments for companies to address via email, or other suitable communication methods as determined by the Government. Benefits of the CSO process and the potential for award include: A streamlined application process requiring only minimal corporate and technical information for fast-track evaluation timelines for solution briefs. Negotiable payment terms for non-dilutive capital. Negotiable intellectual property (IP) rights. Secure and direct feedback from end users, mission partners, and users within the DoD to help product teams develop and hone product design and functionality. Each proposal is evaluated on its individual merits rather than on a comparative basis. Quality Assurance & Acceptance Criteria 8.1 Quality Assurance (QA) All work shall be performed by qualified personnel with documented experience in marine systems. Contractor shall maintain a QA plan that includes: Pre- and post-inspection checklists Calibration of tools and test equipment Documentation of all test results and measurements NPS shall be granted access to inspect work at any stage. 8.2 Acceptance Criteria Each work package shall be considered complete when the following conditions are met: Engines: Start reliably, reach rated RPM, and pass sea trial performance metrics. Navigation Systems: Fully functional with charts loaded and operator training completed. Structural Work: Coatings meet

watertight. SOPs & Labeling: Clear, accurate, and approved by NPS; placards installed and legible. Transport & Training: Vessel delivered without damage; training completed with documentation. Final acceptance shall be granted upon successful walkthrough and NPS sign-off. 9. Deliverables The Contractor shall provide the following: Rebuilt engines with calibration certificates and commissioning report Installed navigation and safety systems with user orientation Structural and deck repairs with QA documentation SOPs in printed and digital formats; laminated checklists Placard layout plan, samples, and as-built labeling diagram Transport plan, insurance certificates, and condition reports Training agenda, attendance roster, and certificates of completion Final acceptance report signed by NPS 10. Warranty Workmanship: Minimum 12 months or 1,000 operating hours (whichever occurs first) on all labor and installed components. Transport & Training: 12-month warranty on training content and delivery; contractor support available for clarification. Materials: Manufacturer warranties apply to all equipment, electronics, and materials supplied. ===== FILE: files/Materials_unpacked/[Content_Types].xml ===== <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?> <Types xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlf

forms_signatures.text: ===== FILE: files/B08_Attachment_02_Price_Schedule_and_Forms_to_Submit_with_Quote.docx ===== PRICE SCHEDULE - INSTRUCTIONS This document serves as a general template. The contractor shall factor the lump sum price to include all labor, tools, equipment, materials, mobilization-in, mobilization-out, necessary for completing all work at the Contractor’s facility. All work shall be performed in accordance with these terms and conditions, including the materials specifications in attachments of this document. The Offeror shall submit a price for all line items below. Failure to do so may render the quote non-responsive. The Government anticipates being able to evaluate solely based upon lump sum prices quoted for each line item. However, the Government reserves the right to request breakdowns of any quoted lump sum prices, such as mobilization in and out, materials, labor, overhead, or profit. On lump sum line items, provide total price only. If no line item exists for a portion of the work, include the cost in a relative line item. In case of error in summation, the total of the corrected line-item amount governs. Round totals and extended prices to the nearest whole dollar (no cents). Award will be made to one contractor in accordance with solicitation. In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) provision, 52.204-07, Quoters must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number and an active registration in the System for Award Management database (SAM.gov) at time of submitting quote. Information about obtaining a UEI number and registration in SAM.gov can be found at: https://sam.gov/content/entity-registration https://sam.gov Fill out the following and submit with quote: Business Name: SAM.gov UEI: Point of Contact Name: Email Address: Mailing Address: Pho

FAR 52.217-2, Cancellation Under Multi-Year Contracts (Oct 1995): If this could become a multi-year contract, this protects the government's right to cancel future years. The classifications are listed in alphabetical order under rate identifiers indicating whether the particular rate is a union rate (current union negotiated rate), a survey rate, a weighted union average rate, a state adopted rate, or a supplemental classification rate. Union Rate Identifiers A four-letter identifier beginning with characters other than SU , UAVG , SA , or SC denotes that a union rate was prevailing for that classification in the survey. Example: PLUM0198-005 07/01/2024. PLUM is an identifier of the union whose collectively bargained rate prevailed in the survey for this classification, which in this example would be Plumbers. 0198 indicates the local union number or district council number where applicable, i.e., Plumbers Local 0198. The next number, 005 in the example, is an internal number used in processing the wage determination. The date, 07/01/2024 in the example, is the effective date of the most current negotiated rate. The Center for Army Analysis (CAA) seeks proposals for an innovative Information Technology (IT) services solution to enhance agency-wide IT and desktop support across its internally managed classified Closed Restricted Network (CRN) and its externally managed classified and unclassified network environments. Offerors shall provide a detailed narrative demonstrating their organizational capacity and a proven record of delivering effective, efficient support services comparable in scope to this requirement. The term innovative is defined as any technology, process, or method, including research and development that is new as of the date of proposal submission, or any new application of an existing technology, process or method as of the proposal date. Under this CSO, the DoD may seek solution briefs, presentations/pitches, and/or proposals from traditional and nontraditional business entities for innovative commercial products, technologies, and services, or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial products, technologies, and services to meet U.S. Army needs and improve readiness. These include, but are not limited to, IT modernization, enhanced cybersecurity, efficient artifact restoration and conservation, streamlined base operations, and improved facility support. This CSO may result in the award of various types of contracts, which may include, but are not limited to, commercially-available products, technologies, or services immediately available; commercially-available products, technologies, or services fueled by commercial or strategic investment; and concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial products, technologies, or services, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for broad defense applications. ars have been reserved for awards under this CSO. The participating DoD agencies will provide no funding for direct reimbursement of white paper or proposal development costs. NOTE: During any step of the CSO, the Government may send written questions or comments for companies to address via email, or other suitable communication methods as determined by the Government. Benefits of the CSO process and the potential for award include: A streamlined application process requiring only minimal corporate and technical information for fast-track evaluation timelines for solution briefs. Negotiable payment terms for non-dilutive capital. Negotiable intellectual property (IP) rights. Secure and direct feedback from end users, mission partners, and users within the DoD to help product teams develop and hone product design and functionality. Each proposal is evaluated on its individual merits rather than on a comparative basis. Contractor personnel are required to wear or prominently display installation identification badges or contractor-furnished contractor identification badges while visiting or performing work on the installation. Contractor personnel shall identify themselves as Contractors during meetings, telephone conversations, in electronic messages, or correspondence related to this contract. The contractor shall submit a written request on company letterhead to the contracting officer listing the following: contract number, location of work site, start and stop dates, and names of employees and subcontractor employees needing access to the base or installation. The letter will also specify the individual(s) authorized to sign for a request for base or installation identification credentials or vehicle passes. The contracting officer will endorse the request and forward it to the issuing base pass and registration office or Security Forces/Police for processing. When reporting to the registration/security police office, the authorized contractor individual(s) should provide a valid driver’s license, current vehicle registration, valid vehicle insurance certificate, and comply with local security procedures to obtain a vehicle pass. During perf

mpt return of credentials and vehicle passes for any employee who no longer requires access to the work site. Upon completion or termination of the contract or expiration of the identification passes/badges, the prime contractor shall ensure that all base or installation identification passes issued to employees and subcontractor employees are returned to the issuing office. The contractor shall provide an after-hours contact number or after-hours email in the Emergency Mass Notification System (EMNS) for each of their personnel, whose normal place of duty is on a DoW installation or within a DoW facility.
